issue.title: GitHub Copilot fails when fetching redirects, even to direct links to raw files, even on GitHub.
issue.body:
GitHub Copilot can't even seem to fetch redirected data from GitHub itself, and it fails silently.

I asked the LLM in Agent mode (I redacted my short intro paragraph here and below):

> #fetch https://github.com/jordial/datimprint/raw/refs/heads/main/cli/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/cli/DatimprintCli.java and https://github.com/jordial/datimprint/raw/refs/heads/main/file/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/file/PathChecker.java and https://github.com/jordial/datimprint/raw/refs/heads/main/file/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/file/PathImprintGenerator.java

The debug window shows that the agent response was:

```
🛠️ fetch_webpage (call_…) {
  "query": "Datimprint CLI and PathChecker classes",
  "urls": [
    "https://github.com/jordial/datimprint/raw/refs/heads/main/cli/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/cli/DatimprintCli.java",
    "https://github.com/jordial/datimprint/raw/refs/heads/main/file/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/file/PathChecker.java",
    "https://github.com/jordial/datimprint/raw/refs/heads/main/file/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/file/PathImprintGenerator.java"
  ]
```

The `fetch_webpage` tool then responded with this (from the debug view):

```
Here is some relevant context from the web page https://github.com/jordial/datimprint/raw/refs/heads/main/file/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/file/PathChecker.java:
The webpage has redirected to "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jordial/datimprint/refs/heads/main/file/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/file/PathChecker.java". Use the vscode_fetchWebPage_internal again to get its contents.
Here is some relevant context from the web page https://github.com/jordial/datimprint/raw/refs/heads/main/cli/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/cli/DatimprintCli.java:
The webpage has redirected to "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jordial/datimprint/refs/heads/main/cli/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/cli/DatimprintCli.java". Use the vscode_fetchWebPage_internal again to get its contents.
Here is some relevant context from the web page https://github.com/jordial/datimprint/raw/refs/heads/main/file/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/file/PathImprintGenerator.java:
The webpage has redirected to "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jordial/datimprint/refs/heads/main/file/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/file/PathImprintGenerator.java". Use the vscode_fetchWebPage_internal again to get its contents.
```

Then it looks like GitHub Copilot resubmitted the request to the LLM with the URLs updated:

```
These attachments may have useful context for the user's query. The user may refer to these attachments directly using a term that starts with #.
<attachment tool="#fetch">
Here is some relevant context from the web page https://github.com/jordial/datimprint/raw/refs/heads/main/file/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/file/PathChecker.java:
The webpage has redirected to "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jordial/datimprint/refs/heads/main/file/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/file/PathChecker.java". Use the vscode_fetchWebPage_internal again to get its contents.
Here is some relevant context from the web page https://github.com/jordial/datimprint/raw/refs/heads/main/cli/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/cli/DatimprintCli.java:
The webpage has redirected to "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jordial/datimprint/refs/heads/main/cli/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/cli/DatimprintCli.java". Use the vscode_fetchWebPage_internal again to get its contents.
Here is some relevant context from the web page https://github.com/jordial/datimprint/raw/refs/heads/main/file/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/file/PathImprintGenerator.java:
The webpage has redirected to "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jordial/datimprint/refs/heads/main/file/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/file/PathImprintGenerator.java". Use the vscode_fetchWebPage_internal again to get its contents.
</attachment>
<prompt>
…

#fetch https://github.com/jordial/datimprint/raw/refs/heads/main/cli/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/cli/DatimprintCli.java and https://github.com/jordial/datimprint/raw/refs/heads/main/file/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/file/PathChecker.java and https://github.com/jordial/datimprint/raw/refs/heads/main/file/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/file/PathImprintGenerator.java
</prompt>
```

Unfortunately the assistant just responded:

```
I'll fetch those files to see your examples of directory traversal and checksum generation.

<fetch_web_page>
<url>https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jordial/datimprint/refs/heads/main/cli/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/cli/DatimprintCli.java</url>
</fetch_web_page>

<fetch_web_page>
<url>https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jordial/datimprint/refs/heads/main/file/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/file/PathChecker.java</url>
</fetch_web_page>

<fetch_web_page>
<url>https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jordial/datimprint/refs/heads/main/file/src/main/java/com/jordial/datimprint/file/PathImprintGenerator.java</url>
</fetch_web_page>
```

And all I see in the chat is that it fetched 3 resources (apparently the first three actual requests, because it never asked for my verification of the content), and then this:

> I'll fetch those files to see your examples of directory traversal and checksum generation.

Thus redirection of fetch seems broken. This is essential functionality. Being unable to fetch files really breaks my workflow. This is a larger problem; see #274925, #248453, and even microsoft/vscode#283164 (opened months ago!).

Note also the irony that I went to the trouble of providing the "raw" file content URLs because GitHub Copilot couldn't even find the file content on the normal user-facing page in GitHub, as noted in other tickets. One would think that providing the "raw" link link would have worked around the problem of waiting for the content to load or for the content to be lost within the page layout, but I didn't factor in that GitHub Copilot might not be able to handle an HTTP redirect. 😕

Please raise the priority of this. If you don't have enough resources, let me know where I can send my resume to join your team and help get this done. I'm serious on all points.

issue.body:

<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.95
- OS Version: Linux x64 5.15.0-139-generic

When _Editor: Detect Indentation_ is enabled and there are some areas indented using 2 spaces, VSCode detects a 2-space indentation even when the file is mostly indented with 4 spaces.


![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/95db4482-c9d4-44c2-896e-1e05014a12f5)

This doesn't happen for other pairs of values such as {3, 6} or {4,8}.
Is there any reason for choosing 2 spaces over 4? Why does this happen only for the {2, 4} pair?

issue.title: Auto-approve GitHub Copilot non-destructive `sed` usage.
issue.body:
As I understand it (I'm not a `sed` expert), only the `sed -i` command is destructive. All other usages are read-only.

The LLM often needs to use `sed` to search files. I shouldn't be bothered for file searches. But I do want to know if the LLM is using `sed` to edit a file.

For example the LLM needed to look up the source code of my own GlobalMentor library in order to refactor the code to use one of its utilities. The source code is in another directory tree. I provided instructions on how to find it. So the LLM issued this benign command (part of path redacted):

```bash
sed -n '140,160p' /…/globalmentor-base/core/src/main/java/com/globalmentor/java/Objects.java
```

That's fine. I shouldn't be bothered with that. Unfortunately the auto-approve setting for `sed` is not granular enough: it says "Always Allow Command: sed".

**Please add a way to specify "Always allow `sed` except when used with the `-i` option.".**

The implementation may require normalization of the CLI command line, as laid out in #281779.

This is related to #276212.

Unfortunately the auto-approve setting for `sed` is not granular enough: it says "Always Allow Command: sed". **Please add a way to specify "Always allow `sed` except when used with the `-i` option.".** The implementation may require normalization of the CLI command line, as laid out in #281779. This is related to #276212.

issue.title: $msCompile fails to match indented dotnet output
issue.body:
Type: Bug TL;DR: `dotnet` (sometimes?) indents error messages with a few leading spaces and this breaks the `$msCompiler` matcher. The `$msCompile` matcher doesn't work on the output from the following task: ```json { "label": "build", "type": "process", "command": "dotnet", "linux": { "args": [ "build", "--no-restore", "-p:TargetRuntimeIdentifier=linux-x64" ] }, "windows": { "args": [ "build", "--no-restore", "-p:TargetRuntimeIdentifier=win-x64" ], }, "options": { "cwd": "${workspaceFolder:SiteGen}" }, "echoCommand": true, "problemMatcher": "$msCompile", "presentation": { "reveal": "never", "panel": "dedicated", "clear": true, "revealProblems": "onProblem", }, "group": { "kind": "build", "isDefault": true } }, ``` However, swapping out the `problemMatcher` with the following _does_ work (on both Windows and Linux): ```json "problemMatcher": { "base": "$msCompile", "pattern":[ { "regexp": "^\\s*(?:\\s*\\d+>)?(\\S.*)\\((\\d+|\\d+,\\d+|\\d+,\\d+,\\d+,\\d+)\\)\\s*:\\s+((?:fatal +)?error|warning|info)\\s+(\\w+\\d+)\\s*:\\s*(.*)$", "kind": "location", "file": 1, "location": 2, "severity": 3, "code": 4, "message": 5 } ] }, ``` The `regexp` is taken verbatim from [your own source here](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/614287f64de39de2b2b2b9b185867187a150d0bb/src/vs/workbench/contrib/tasks/common/problemMatcher.ts#L1500), except I've added a `\s*` at the beginning. issue.title: Support calling additional `resolveDebugConfiguration` callbacks if one callback changes the debug configuration `type`
issue.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

Today, VSCode's debug configuration provider API provides partial support for extensions that change the `type` property on a debug configuration returned by the `resolveDebugConfiguration` on a provider. The support today includes activating debuggers for the new debug configuration `type`. This support was added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/4150347750b762a3f537ef660e96617083260066 to fix https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/135090.

However, this support does not include running the `resolveDebugConfiguration` callback for configuration providers keyed off the new `type`. This would be desireable for extensions that run highly customized debug configurations whose resolved configuration's `type` may differ depending on other installed extensions, target platform, or on user input.

I would be willing to contribute an implementation of this feature if the idea is amenable.

issue.title: `FindTextInFiles` doesn't support comma-separated globs with {}

tasks.query:
`FindTextInFiles` doesn't support comma-separated globs with {}

Try extension with: ```typescript const disposable = vscode.commands.registerCommand('extension.helloWorld', async () => { const results: string[] = []; const glob = await vscode.window.showInputBox({ prompt: 'Glob pattern' }); await vscode.workspace.findTextInFiles({ pattern: 'foo' }, { include: new vscode.RelativePattern(vscode.workspace.workspaceFolders![0], glob!), }, r => results.push(r.uri.toString())); vscode.window.showInformationMessage(JSON.stringify(results)); }); ``` ...and a workspace with files a/hello.txt and b/hello.txt both containing foo. Entering a glob for `a/*.*` or `b/*.*` will work, but `{a/*.*,b/*.*}` will return no results. `{a/*.*,b/*.*}` is a valid glob and should work

issue.title: Prepending PATH env var with environmentVariableCollection doesn't work on macOS
issue.body:
This was covered a little bit in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/94153 but that issue is locked and can't be discussed there. This feature feels pretty broken on macOS and I hope might be revisited.

The issue is on macOS prepending to `PATH`:

```
context.environmentVariableCollection.prepend("PATH", "/foo/my/path:");
```

This ends up being added to the end of the path, rather than the start. @Tyriar wrote up why this is in microsoft/vscode-docs@38653d4 and offered two workarounds, however neither of them are usable in my testing (as well as not really being feasible to tell all users to change):

- `"terminal.integrated.inheritEnv": false` makes no difference at all, the PATH till is added to the end (this is a problem because the purpose of using `prepend` above is that we need to override any existing SDK on PATH with the one the user just selected)
- `"terminal.integrated.shellArgs": []` results in a completely empty `PATH` besides the values I've prepended, which means that pretty much everything else is missing and won't work. This might be solvable by pushing `process.env.PATH` into `environmentVariableCollection` too, however the prompt to the user would look ridiculous as it would include their entire PATH

I appreciate this probably isn't VS Code's fault, but given macOS is fairly common and this behaviour seems to happen on a clean macOS install (it happens on both of mine, and I've customised almost nothing) it feels like it's worth trying to fix (maybe even if it means sending `export PATH=foo:$PATH` once the shell is initialised? 😄).

issue.title: Allow extensions to get the current editor layout
issue.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
When developing a extension I am using `vscode.setEditorLayout` as described in https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/commands, and I am able to set editor layout/groups:

```javascript
vscode.commands.executeCommand(
  'vscode.setEditorLayout',
  { orientation: 1, groups: [{size: 0.4 }, { size: 0.6 }], }
);
```

The problem is that, before setting the layout, sometimes is good the get the current state, so we don't mess with the current displayed layout: 

```javascript
let layout = vscode.window.editorLayout 
console.log(layout)
// { orientation: 1, groups: [{size: 0.7 }, { size: 0.3 }], }
```

In the above example we could check that we already have two groups in vertical orientation, and because of that we won't change the size, we will respect the sizes the user already set.

I looked at vscode source code and found IEditorGroupsService, but couldn't find a way for a extension to access it, so sorry if I missed something.

PS: the window.editorLayout is just an idea, I don't know if there is another name or more appropriate namespace for this.
